UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

[PROPOSED] ORDER ESTABLISHING A BRIEFING, SUBMISSION, AND DETERMINATION SCHEDULE FOR THE TWO RULE 26(d)(1) APPLICATIONS

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Administrative Motion for Expedited Briefing, Priority Determination, and a Defined Decision Schedule for the Two Rule 26(d)(1) Applications (ECF No. [___]) (the “Administrative Motion”). The Court has considered the Administrative Motion, the Memorandum in Support, the Administrative Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine, Plaintiff’s Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument and Request for Prompt Determination on the Papers, [any opposition and reply,] and Plaintiff’s request concerning the sequencing of any disposition that would depend on the reporting fact addressed by the applications. It is hereby ORDERED as follows.

1.	Scope. This Order governs Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve One Interrogatory on NCMEC Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name (ECF No. [___]) (the “NCMEC Application”) and Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve Two Interrogatories on Meta Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name and Facebook Account (ECF No. [___]) (the “Meta Application”) (together, the “Applications”).

2.	Administrative disposition. The Administrative Motion is GRANTED to the extent stated in this Order. This Order establishes a schedule only. Whether to authorize any discovery remains for determination in the Applications. Entry of this Order does not authorize discovery, does not authorize service of any interrogatory, does not start any interrogatory-response period, and does not open general discovery. The separate proposed orders submitted with the Applications govern any service and response periods if authorization is granted.

3.	Opposition and reply dates. The dates in this paragraph provide seven calendar days after service of each complete Application for opposition and three calendar days after each opposition deadline for reply. Any opposition to the NCMEC Application must be filed and served by [date]. Plaintiff may file and serve one reply by [date]. Any opposition to the Meta Application must be filed and served by [date]. Plaintiff may file and serve one reply by [date]. These are fixed calendar deadlines. No additional days attach to those dates because of the method of service. Plaintiff may file a reply before its deadline. One reply addresses every timely opposition to that Application. Separate opposition papers do not create additional reply rounds. Defendant Katie Hall may oppose or join an opposition to the NCMEC Application by its opposition date; Hall is not a discovery respondent. The dates for one Application are not affected by the date on which the other Application was docketed or served.

4.	Filing, service, and courtesy copies. Each opposition and reply shall be filed with the Clerk and served under Rule 5. Each party filing an opposition or reply under this Order shall also send a contemporaneous electronic courtesy copy to each other party, in addition to service under Rule 5; Plaintiff’s address for that purpose is jayballentine@protonmail.com. Courtesy delivery does not constitute consent to electronic service under Rule 5(b)(2)(E) and starts no period.

5.	Submission. Each Application becomes submitted when its opposition deadline has passed and Plaintiff has filed and served the authorized reply or the reply deadline has passed. If no opposition is filed, the Application becomes submitted when its opposition deadline passes. Neither Application awaits briefing or determination of the other. An early reply does not close another party’s opposition period. The Court may act on an Application earlier when procedurally appropriate. A late filing does not automatically restart briefing or the determination period; any change to this schedule requires direction of the Court. An Application that is fully briefed when this Order is entered keeps its completed briefing and is submitted upon entry of this Order.

6.	Determination on the papers. Each Application will be determined on the papers under Rule 78(b) and Local Civil Rule 7(J). No notice of hearing is required for submission under this Order, subject to further direction of the Court.

7.	Determination. Each Application will be determined within seven calendar days after it becomes submitted, unless a further order fixes a different date certain for that Application and states the reason for the different date.

8.	Routing. The District Judge retains determination of the requested limited exceptions to the deferral described in ECF No. 108, including any service and response terms, as to both Applications.

9.	Sequencing. To the extent an adverse disposition would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by an Application’s Exhibit A, the Court will resolve that authorization request before or expressly within that disposition.

10.	Independence. Neither Application awaits completion of briefing or determination of the other. Neither Application awaits determination of the pending amendment, summary-judgment, settlement-referral, objection, reconsideration, or clarification proceedings.

11.	Preservation. This Order disposes of the Administrative Motion only to the extent expressly stated. This Order does not determine either Application’s merits or dispose of any other pending motion or objection. This Order grants no discovery authorization, opens no general discovery, imposes no general stay, permits no amendment, and makes no finding concerning the merits of any claim or defense or the existence, contents, source, or accuracy of any CyberTipline report. Neither an opposition, nor silence, nor the allocation of determination under this Order establishes report existence or discovery entitlement.

12.	Prospective safeguards. No deadline imposed by this Order operates retroactively. Completed briefing remains complete. This Order does not automatically restart briefing, revive an expired deadline, or enlarge an existing deadline. Any prospective replacement date must be stated expressly in this Order. The fixed dates in paragraph 3 govern only the briefing of the Applications; this Order changes no deadline to object under Rule 72, no discovery-response period, and no deadline in any other proceeding.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026

______________________________

Rossie D. Alston, Jr.

United States District Judge
